config.title: Forms & Validation

intro.title: Forms & Validation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a user registration form that collects a name and email address. You'll learn how to create and manage form inputs using Vue's v-model directive for two-way data binding. The core concept is form validation, where you'll implement real-time feedback to check if the email is valid and if required fields are filled. You'll use Vue's reactive state and computed properties to handle validation logic and display error messages, giving you hands-on experience with form handling in Vue applications.
intro.usecase: Forms with validation are essential in nearly every interactive web application. You'll implement this pattern when building user registration forms, checkout processes in e-commerce sites, or data entry interfaces in admin dashboards. For example, when users sign up for a service, you need to validate email formats, password strength, and required fields before submission. In Vue, you'll create reactive form components that provide immediate feedback when users enter invalid data, preventing errors and improving user experience.

objectives: Construct a form in Vue using v-model to bind input fields to reactive data properties.
Implement form validation by applying computed properties or watchers to check user input against defined rules.
Configure conditional rendering to display validation error messages based on the state of the form data.
Integrate form submission handling by preventing default browser behavior and processing validated data.
Manipulate form state to reset input fields and clear validation errors upon successful submission.
Initialize a Vue component with reactive data structures suitable for managing multiple form fields and their validation status.

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a module
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and ref from 'vue' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported, enabling reactive state management.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Define a Vue component named 'FormValidation' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can create a component by defining a function that returns an object. The setup function is where you'll handle reactive state and logic.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue' here

// Define the FormValidation component with a setup function
steps.expectedOutcome: The component is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object, ready for adding reactive state and form logic.
successCriteria: A component named 'FormValidation' is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a component named 'FormValidation' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition isn't quite right. Remember to create a component named 'FormValidation' with a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize form data state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your FormValidation component, create a reactive formData object using ref with name and email properties, both initialized as empty strings.
steps.hint: Use ref to create reactive state. The formData object should have name and email properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The formData reactive object is created with name and email properties, both initialized as empty strings.
successCriteria: A formData reactive object is created using ref with name and email properties set to empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure formData is created using ref and has both name and email properties initialized as empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the setup function, use ref to create a formData object with name and email properties, both set to empty strings.

steps.title: Initialize validation errors state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive errors object using ref to store validation messages. Initialize it as an empty object.
steps.hint: Use ref({}) to create a reactive errors object that will hold validation error messages for each form field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: reactive state for errors
const errors = ref({});
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive errors object is initialized in the component's setup function, ready to store validation error messages.
successCriteria: The errors object is created using ref and initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref to create a reactive errors object initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The errors object wasn't properly created. Use ref({}) inside the setup function to initialize it.

steps.title: Define the validateForm function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named validateForm that validates the name and email fields and updates the errors state.
steps.hint: The validateForm function should check if name is empty and if email contains an '@' symbol, then update the errors object accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a validateForm function that validates the name and email fields and updates the errors reactive object.
successCriteria: The validateForm function is defined inside setup, checks both name and email fields, and updates errors.value with appropriate error messages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your validateForm function checks both name and email fields and properly updates the errors.value object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateForm function should be defined inside the setup function and should validate both name and email fields, updating the errors state with appropriate messages.

steps.title: Define the handleSubmit function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleSubmit that calls validateForm and logs the form data if valid.
steps.hint: Create a function that first validates the form, then checks if there are any errors before processing the data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSubmit function is defined that validates the form and logs the form data when valid.
successCriteria: The handleSubmit function is defined, calls validateForm, checks for errors, and logs formData.value when valid.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handleSubmit function. Make sure it calls validateForm and logs formData.value only when there are no errors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function is missing or incomplete. It should validate the form and log the data when valid.

steps.title: Add the form container and heading
steps.instruction: In the return object of your setup function, add a form container div with a heading element that says 'Contact Form'.
steps.hint: The return object should contain a template. Inside the template, add a div element with a class of 'form-container', and inside that div, add an h1 element with the text 'Contact Form'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now return a basic form structure with a container and heading, ready for form fields to be added in subsequent steps.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with a template property containing a div with class 'form-container' and an h1 with text 'Contact Form'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the container div with class 'form-container' and the h1 element with the text 'Contact Form' in your template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure isn't complete. Check that you're returning a template with a div containing an h1 element.

steps.title: Add name input field with v-model binding
steps.instruction: Inside the form container, add a text input field for the name with v-model binding to formData.name. Include a label for the input.
steps.hint: Use the <input> element with type='text' and bind it to formData.name using v-model. Add a <label> element with 'Name:' text before the input.
steps.expectedOutcome: A text input field for the name appears in the form, bound to the formData.name reactive property with a label.
successCriteria: The template includes a <label> with 'Name:' text and an <input type="text"> element with v-model="formData.name" binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but make sure it has both the v-model binding to formData.name and a proper label.
steps.feedbackWrong: The name input field is missing or doesn't have the correct v-model binding. Check that you're using v-model="formData.name" with a text input.

steps.title: Add email input field with v-model binding
steps.instruction: Add an email input field to your form with v-model binding to formData.email, similar to the name input you already created.
steps.hint: Add an <input> element with type='email' and use v-model to bind it to formData.email. Place it after the name input.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding an input to reactive data
<input type="email" v-model="formData.email" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have an email input field that updates the formData.email value when the user types.
successCriteria: An email input field with v-model binding to formData.email is added to the form.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but make sure it has type='email' and v-model binding to formData.email.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email input field with v-model binding is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add submit button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a submit button inside the form that calls the handleSubmit function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use a <button> element with type='submit' and @click='handleSubmit'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a submit button
<button type="submit" @click="handleSubmit">Submit Form</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A submit button appears in the form that triggers form submission when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element has type='submit' and @click='handleSubmit'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has type='submit' and @click='handleSubmit'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the required attributes. Try adding a <button> with type='submit' and @click='handleSubmit'.
